svg.title: Savitsky decision tree: increase or decrease a design variable
svg.desc: Nine variable heads, each splitting into increase and decrease. Follow geometry, coefficients, forces, then coupled equilibrium and final power. Algebraic signs hold with other independent quantities fixed and within the conditions stated. Competing effects and final equilibrium directions are marked depends. No operating-point examples are used.
svg.text: Choose a head → follow INCREASE or DECREASE → trace the algebra → distinguish a direct effect from the combined equilibrium response.
BLUE = increase · ORANGE = decrease · White = direct effects at fixed τ, Lk and other inputs · Purple = combined response · ? = no universal sign
Conditions: positive speed, positive lift / friction, 0 < τ < 90°, cos(τ + ε) > 0. Geometry arrows assume wet chines Lc > 0 and 0 < β < 90°; stop at branch or validity limits.
Re: λb and fv both vary

HOW STRONGLY DOES EACH CHANGING TERM RESPOND?
For y = Cxⁿ: a small relative change in x produces approximately n times that relative change in y. Linear: +1 → 1×; quadratic: +2 → 2×; square root: +½ → ½×; inverse: −1 → reversed 1×.

These labels compare percentage sensitivity with other factors fixed. S = Ab − Bb² and λ = Lk/b − c are sums, so their full sensitivity is not a single exponent. Competing paths require combining their contributions.

Monotonic arrows apply only while the stated regime persists. A large change can reach dry chines, nonphysical lift or an empirical limit; a different formula branch may then apply. No planing-onset prediction is supplied.

Notation: L = lift; Lk / Lc = wetted keel / chine lengths; λ = mean wet length / beam; xp = pressure center; zf = friction-force height; fv = bottom-flow speed ratio squared. Constants C, A, B and c hold other factors fixed.
